newsitem.title: USA: McVeigh wants prosecution to call him "Mister".
newsitem.headline: McVeigh wants prosecution to call him "Mister".

text.p: Lawyers for accused Oklahoma City bomber Timothy McVeigh want the prosecution to treat him with respect and call him "Mister," according to court papers.
A defence motion filed last week but made public Tuesday calls on presiding Judge Richard Matsch to order prosecutors to stop calling the defendant "McVeigh" and start calling him "Mr. McVeigh."
The motion said that prosecutors, by not calling him "Mister," are sending a "pernicious signal" to the jury that the defendant is guilty.

"Left uncured, disrespect of this sort may subtly incline jurors toward a guilty verdict. Additionally, the effect of singling our Mr McVeigh for discourtesy is a small but significant step toward dehumanizing and demonising him before jurors who may later be called upon to assess a penalty in this case," the motion said.

The motion added that McVeigh deserved to be addressed as "Mister" because under American law a defendant is innocent until proved guilty. He has pleaded innocent to charges of making and setting off the bomb that destroyed the Alfred P. Murrah federal building on April 19, 1995, taking 168 lives.
Chief prosecutor Joseph Hartzler repeatedly referred to the defendant as McVeigh in his opening statement.
Prosecutors were not immediately available for comment and it was not clear when Judge Matsch would rule on the motion.
